$comment: TEMPLATE FILE — read this variant's own top-level README.md before editing. This hook blocks a Claude Code session from committing directly to main/master. It is git-tracked, so it is live automatically in every fresh clone/worktree of this project — no manual install step, unlike a real .git/hooks/pre-commit (which requires a per-checkout `cp` and reliably lags days-to-never behind bootstrap). Two edge cases, both handled explicitly rather than left to fail open: (1) a brand-new repo's unborn HEAD, before any commit exists — `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` errors on this and would leave the branch check silently unable to fire; fixed by using `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` instead, which resolves the branch name correctly in both the unborn and normal case. (2) this project isn't a git repository at all yet (e.g. this variant was copied into a plain folder before `git init` ran) — rather than silently allow (the gate simply can't reason about branches with no repo, so doing nothing would look like protection while providing none), this asks for explicit confirmation with a visible warning instead, on the principle that a gate whose failure mode is silent is not proven until it's been made to fail loudly. Extend the same PreToolUse array with further checks (e.g. a review-artifact-required-before-merge gate) as this project's own workflow needs them -- APPEND them rather than prepending, because .claude/hooks/selftest-branch-guard.sh reads the first "Bash"-matcher group and would otherwise report a confusing red against a perfectly good gate; each new BINDING rule you add here should ship with this kind of mechanical check in the same change, or be labeled advisory instead. Known sharp edge, confirmed live in dogfooding: this check reads the branch you're on BEFORE the whole Bash command runs, so `git switch feature-x && git commit ...` in one call is denied against your old branch even though the commit would have landed correctly on the new one after the switch — run the switch as its own command first (see CLAUDE.md's repository-etiquette section).
$comment-rm-rf: Second gate in the same PreToolUse array, added by the worked example's rung 3 (see templates/base-project-worked-example/README.md, «Ступень 3»). It denies `rm -rf` when the target is something the SHELL expands rather than something you wrote out: a glob (`*`, `?`), a tilde, or a variable. That is the line, and it is drawn there on purpose — `rm -rf dist` states its own blast radius and is allowed; `rm -rf dist/*`, `rm -rf $DIR` and `rm -rf ~/` hand that decision to expansion at delete time, which is the shape of the reported incident behind this gate (an agent asked to clean up an old repository ran `rm -rf tests/ patches/ plan/ ~/` — docker.com/blog/coding-agent-horror-stories-the-rm-rf-incident). Deliberately built from the same jq | read -r | grep pieces as the branch guard above, so it inherits the same two blind spots: a prefixed invocation (`/bin/rm -rf *`) is not the literal word `rm` at a statement start, and `read -r` sees only the first line of a multi-line command. A third is its own: the flags must arrive as one cluster, so `rm -r -f x/*` passes. All three are demonstrated with output by .claude/hooks/selftest-branch-guard.sh, which covers this hook as well as the branch guard and reports them as LIMIT lines, never as passes. This gate filters one command shape. It is a discipline aid whose limits are named, not a barrier. One limit of THIS KEY, stated because a file whose preamble warns that a hook can fail silently should not carry an unstated one of its own: whether Claude Code tolerates a second, non-standard top-level key next to $comment has not been verified live. $comment is itself an unrecognised key the upstream template already relies on, so the risk is the same class — but same-class is not tested. `jq -r 'keys[]' .claude/settings.json` in this repository prints `hooks` alone: both files carrying $comment live under templates/ and are never loaded, so neither key has live evidence behind it. If a future version rejects unknown keys, move both texts to a file beside this one; neither hook depends on either key.

hooks.command: jq -r '.tool_input.command' | { read -r cmd; if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|]\s*)git\s+commit\b'; then if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"WARNING: branch-protection gate inactive \u2014 this is not a git repository yet (no .git found), so this hook cannot check anything. Run git init before your first commit if you want main/master protection; proceeding now commits with no branch discipline in effect."}}'; exit 0; fi; branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null); if [ "$branch" = "main" ] || [ "$branch" = "master" ]; then echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED: direct commit to main/master. Create a feature branch first."}}'; exit 0; fi; fi; }

jq -r '.tool_input.command' | { read -r cmd; if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|]\s*)rm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*-[a-zA-Z]*([rR][a-zA-Z]*f|f[a-zA-Z]*[rR])[a-zA-Z]*\s+[^;&|]*[*?~$]'; then echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED: `rm -rf` whose target the shell expands (`*`, `?`, `~`, `$VAR`) instead of naming. What gets deleted is then decided at run time, not in the command you approved: `rm -rf $BUILD_DIR/*` with BUILD_DIR unset is `rm -rf /*`, and the incident this gate exists for ended in `rm -rf tests/ patches/ plan/ ~/`. Write out the paths you mean."}}'; exit 0; fi; }
